newsitem.title: UK: LME copper, defences eroded, ends weak near lows.
newsitem.headline: LME copper, defences eroded, ends weak near lows.

text.p: Copper prices lurched lower in Thursday afternoon LME trading with Wednesday's break below $1,900 followed by fresh technical sales and liquidation.
Traders said the market was hit by bearish sentiment, given the speed at which prices have fallen from early September peaks of $2,165, and further losses are on the cards.
During the afternoon rings and kerb prices held close to $1,850 but any further decline will usher in more pain in the shape of option delta sales.
"It is on a bit of a knife-edge at the moment. It was protected to some extent between $1,850/60, but short-term we see it testing $1,825 and $1,800," one trader said.
Copper spreads continue to give no cause for concern, with few premiums between now and October and the overall cash/threes backwardation at just $10/12.
Final three months business was at $1,852 a tonne, just $1.50 above the low, but a hefty $63 down from Wednesday's kerb.
The pressure on the red metal followed losses in aluminium on Wednesday and resulted in negative sentiment spreading through most other metals.
Aluminium notched another two-year low, hitting $1,429 at one point, although it was noticeable that there was some buying interest attracted by the extent of the decline this week.
Levels under $1,430 sparked some covering and prices closed the kerb at $1,435, still down $3.50 from Wednesday. Another stock increase is expected on Friday, traders said.
Nickel followed the trend and continued to re-trace from Wednesday's 2-1/2 month peaks, although there was an undercurrent of caution over a brief stoppage at Russia's Norilsk on Thursday.
Traders said this factor, and Inco/union talks reaching a crucial point at Manitoba in Canada, suggest the immediate downside is protected. Last kerb trade was at $7,560, down $75.
Zinc occasionally threatened to test the $1,000 level on the downside, but was cushioned on dips by trade support. Last business was at $1,017, a $8 gain from yesterday.
Lead business was slow throughout the day, and routine trading fluctuations tended to reflect the trend. Prices edged up on the kerb to close at $815, a $1 advance.
Tin perked up on the kerb although the market remained depressed by earlier losses after losing its hold on $6,200 this week. Three months finished at $6,140, a $65 loss on the day.
Alloy was little changed when traded and closed a subdued session at $1,240/44 a tonne against $1,245 last Wednesday. --Martin Hayes, london Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
